analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture depicts a scalable video rendering backend leveraging EC2 spot instances and AWS serverless components. 1. Request submission & status: User requests pass through API Gateway to a validation Lambda, which places rendering jobs onto SQS #1. Completed job notifications are sent from EC2 workers to SQS #2, triggering the validation Lambda to notify the user. 2. Rendering pipeline: EC2 spot instances consume jobs from SQS #1, read/write video assets to S3, and output completed video data. 3. Video delivery: CloudFront caches and streams rendered video content from S3 to web/mobile users. 4. Auto scaling orchestration: Step Functions manages scaling operations by executing a Lambda function that evaluates CloudWatch metrics and scales EC2 Auto Scaling groups. 5. Spot termination management: CloudWatch captures spot instance interruption notices and triggers a dedicated Lambda, which alerts EC2 spot workers to drain running jobs and stop receiving new ones. The ledger contains 19 visual connections, and exactly 19 edges have been emitted.
